input.quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: Section 21.1 caps each Party at only one month of Fees actually paid — well below the fallback of 12 months' fees and inside walk-away territory (a cap below six months' fees). The phrase "without exception" also overrides the otherwise sound Excluded Claims regime in 21.2/21.3, pulling indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap with no super-cap. The cap is mutual and 21.3 correctly excludes Customer's payment obligations from "damages", so the minimal edit is to reset the basis to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and delete "without exception" so the existing carve-outs operate.

ops.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, which are not subject to any limitation of liability, each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' Fees or USD 1,000,000, as a one-month cap is far below a meaningful recovery for a USD 2,000,000 per year commitment. We also removed "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims regime in Sections 21.2 and 21.3 (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) sits outside the cap as drafted.
proposal.summary: Raise the mutual liability cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 and preserve the Excluded Claims carve-outs.
